raw_answer_text:
A1: The clk signal (constant "p" pattern) toggles regularly throughout, independent of req/ack/done.
A2: Request, acknowledge, and completion signals all rest at low (0) at the start.
A3: The request signal transitions (asserts) first, before the acknowledge.
A4: No — in the diagram, ack only rises after req has already risen; there is no point where ack goes high while req is still low.
A5: The diagram shows req falling only after ack has risen (and stays high while ack is still asserted); the file does not explicitly state a causal mechanism beyond this timing relationship.
A6: The diagram shows ack falling only after req has already fallen; again, the file shows this timing order but does not explicitly state the cause.
A7: The done signal goes high during the interval after req falls and while ack is still high, then falls again before ack does — the file indicates it marks completion following the req/ack exchange, but does not explain its meaning beyond the waveform timing.
A8: (1) req rises, (2) ack rises, (3) req falls, (4) ack falls.
